tweet_summary: A post shows a slick 'Introducing GPT-6' graphic with the caption 'WHATTTTTT???????' implying OpenAI has announced or released GPT-6.
why_note_decision: The 'Introducing GPT-6' graphic is fake. As of the post date (May 11, 2026) OpenAI's latest model was GPT-5.5 (released April 23, 2026); GPT-6 had not been announced or released. The image is a fabricated/mock announcement. A note clarifying this is warranted, though several replies already suspect it's fake.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note establishes that the GPT-6 announcement graphic is fake/fabricated and that OpenAI has not announced or released GPT-6, with GPT-5.5 being the latest model at the time. A note that treats GPT-6 as a real release FAILS. The correction must name that no such announcement exists; pointing to OpenAI's official channels as the verification path is good practice.
reference_note: The depicted GPT-6 announcement is fake; OpenAI has not released or announced GPT-6, with GPT-5.5 (released April 2026) as the latest model. https://openai.com/blog/ https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9624314-model-release-notes

fact_check.notes: OpenAI released GPT-5.5 (codename Spud) on Apr 23, 2026; GPT-6 was not announced/released as of May 2026 (projected Q3-Q4 2026). The 'Introducing GPT-6' image is a fabricated announcement.

importance.lens_rationale: 211k impressions; a fake AI-product announcement — directly in the AI-progress lens but low real-world consequence since it's quickly self-correcting and obviously a mock-up.
